sources.title: About Broomkit
sources.excerpt: Broomkit is a product of DPR Software Labs OPC Private Limited, designed and built by Diljit PR. It is not a product of Apple Inc., and it is not a rebadged version of any other cleaner. The app is written in Swift and ships as a native macOS application plus a command-line tool. It runs on macOS 14.0 or later, on both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.
sources.scope: Read-only WebFetch; exact request timestamp not emitted, date retained honestly. Vendor statements, not corporate/binary audit.

sources.title: Terms of service
excerpts: Every feature is free for the first 3 days after installation and requires no account, no card and no licence. After that a valid licence is required to use the app.
It runs once per Mac and does not restart on reinstallation.
It is a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use Broomkit on the number of Macs stated on the licence you bought — one.
You may move a licence between machines by deactivating it on one and activating it on another; a seat is concurrent, not permanently bound to the first Mac it touched.
Reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble the application, except where that right cannot lawfully be excluded
Broomkit requires macOS 14.0 or later and Full Disk Access to function as described.
We do not warrant that the software will be uninterrupted or error-free, or that its categorisation of any given file is correct
sources.scope: WebFetch, retained excerpts; no broad image-republication grant found. Use-right restrictions support proprietary treatment, not an open-source licence.

sources.title: Licensing — all sales final
excerpts: After 3 days a licence is required to keep using the app.
The licence never expires and you are never charged again. Scanning continues to work for free either way.
All licence purchases are final. We do not offer refunds, chargebacks by agreement, or ‘try Reclaim then return’ windows.
A validated licence works offline for 14 days before it re-checks

sources.title: Privacy policy
excerpts: Broomkit does not require an account, and never transmits your scan results, file names or file paths anywhere. Scanning happens entirely on your Mac, and the results stay on it.
The app makes two kinds of outbound request, and no others: validating a licence key against Dodo Payments, and an optional once-a-day fetch of a small version file from broomkit.com
The request contains the licence key and the identifier of the Mac it is being activated on
A validated licence works offline for 14 days before it needs to check again.

workflow.title: Review a Mac cleanup list before emptying the Trash
workflow.primaryIntent: Turn a disk map and candidate list into an explicit keep/remove/rebuild decision, rather than treating the headline total as permission.
workflow.distinctAngle: Follow Broomkit's Disk Map → selected paths → review → confirmation sequence as a documented workflow, then distinguish one-off cleanup from investigating recurring growth. Do not write another generic System Data listicle.
sections: Read the map without treating its total as guaranteed recovery
Classify each proposed path: original, regenerable or unknown
Separate app reset/uninstallation from disposable cache
Review Trash moves before deciding whether to empty
Investigate recurring growth instead of repeating deletion
workflow.visualPlan: Cleared Broomkit Disk Map screenshot immediately after lead, then labeled current-source Breathing Room Space preview. Current link-only vendor visual blocks this plan.
workflow.interactionPass: Handoff a local-only keep/remove/rebuild decision checklist: ownership known? backup available? rebuild/download cost understood? app closed where appropriate? unknown personal data stays. No filesystem access, deletion or invented space calculation.
workflow.recommendationBoundary: At most one disclosed recommendation: Breathing Room, which we build, may suit source-based recurring-growth investigation; its preview, hosted AI, Python and signing caveats must remain visible. Broomkit may suit an integrated map/uninstaller workflow with a one-time offer. No hands-on claim.
workflow.length: Earned; normally 900–1800 words only if evidence supports it. No compulsory FAQ or code demo.
